History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Who founded the YMCA College of Physical Education at Madras?

Harry Crowe Buck, an American, founded the college in 1920 and is called the father of modern physical education in India. P.M. Joseph was the first principal of LNCPE Gwalior, G.D. Sondhi is linked with the Asian Games movement, and Dr Tarachand chaired the 1948 committee on physical education.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
In which year was the YMCA College of Physical Education, Madras established?

The college opened in 1920 as the first institution in India to train physical education teachers. 1914 is the year of HVPM Amravati, 1931 is the Government College of Physical Education at Hyderabad, and 1957 is LNCPE Gwalior.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education (now LNIPE), Gwalior was established in

LNCPE was set up in 1957, the centenary year of the 1857 uprising, and named after Rani Lakshmibai. 1961 is the year of NIS Patiala, 1984 of the Sports Authority of India, and 1950 of the Central Advisory Board of Physical Education and Recreation.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Who is known as the father of gymnastics and founder of the Turnverein movement?

Jahn opened the first open-air gymnasium (Turnplatz) at Hasenheide near Berlin in 1811 and started the Turnverein clubs. Guts Muths is called the grandfather of gymnastics, Ling founded the Swedish system and Nachtegall led physical education in Denmark.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Swedish system of gymnastics was developed by

Ling founded the Royal Central Institute of Gymnastics at Stockholm in 1814 and classified gymnastics as educational, military, medical and aesthetic. Jahn and Basedow belong to Germany, and Maclaren worked in Britain.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The phrase "education through the physical" is associated with

Jesse Feiring Williams argued that physical activity is a means to total education, in contrast to the older idea of education of the physical. Bucher and Nash are known for their lists of objectives, and Rousseau for naturalism.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The main aim of education in ancient Sparta was to produce

Sparta was a military state; boys entered the agoge at about seven for harsh physical and military training. Harmony of body and mind with philosophy and arts was the Athenian ideal, not the Spartan one.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
In ancient Athens the palaestra was a

The palaestra was a private school where boys learnt wrestling, boxing and gymnastics under a paidotribe. Older youths went to the gymnasium. Chariot races were held in the hippodrome, and public baths (thermae) belong to Rome.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Philanthropinum, the first school to give physical education a place in the daily timetable, was founded by

Basedow opened the Philanthropinum at Dessau in 1774 on naturalistic lines. Guts Muths taught at Schnepfenthal, Jahn founded the Turnverein, and Spiess introduced gymnastics into German schools later.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Which philosophy says education should follow nature and the natural development of the child?

Naturalism, advocated by Rousseau in Emile, favours play, freedom and learning from nature. Idealism stresses mind and eternal values, pragmatism stresses experience and usefulness, and existentialism stresses individual choice.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
"Learning by doing" is the central idea of

Pragmatism, represented by John Dewey, holds that knowledge comes from experience and problem solving, which suits activity-based physical education. Idealism emphasises ideas, realism the objective world, and naturalism the laws of nature.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
According to Sheldon, a person with a muscular, athletic body build is a

Sheldon classified body types as endomorph (round and fat), mesomorph (muscular) and ectomorph (lean and tall). Pyknic is a term from Kretschmer's classification and corresponds roughly to the endomorph.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Development that proceeds from head to foot is called

Cephalocaudal means head-to-tail: control of the head comes before the trunk and legs. Proximodistal means from the centre of the body outward to the limbs. The other two terms are not directions of growth.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
National Sports Day in India is celebrated on 29 August to mark the birthday of

Hockey wizard Dhyan Chand was born on 29 August 1905. National sports awards are traditionally presented on this day. Milkha Singh and P.T. Usha are athletics legends and K.D. Jadhav was an Olympic medallist in wrestling.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports, Patiala was established in
NIS Patiala was set up in 1961 in the Moti Bagh Palace to train coaches scientifically. 1957 is LNCPE Gwalior and 1984 is the Sports Authority of India, with which NIS was merged in 1987.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Sports Authority of India (SAI) was established in
SAI was set up in 1984 to maintain the infrastructure created for the 1982 Asian Games at New Delhi and to promote sport. 1982 is the year of those Games and 1961 is the year of NIS Patiala.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Rajkumari Amrit Kaur Coaching Scheme was started in

The scheme began in 1953 to give coaching to sportspersons and was later merged into the National Institute of Sports. 1948 is the Tarachand Committee, 1961 is NIS Patiala and 1965 is the National Fitness Corps.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Which committee was appointed in 1959 to coordinate the various schemes of physical education and youth welfare in schools?

The Kunzru Committee examined schemes such as NCC, ACC and the National Discipline Scheme and led to the National Fitness Corps. The Tarachand Committee (1948) recommended a central institute of physical education. The other two are general education commissions.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The Fit India Movement was launched on
The movement was launched by the Prime Minister on National Sports Day, 29 August 2019, to make fitness part of daily life. 21 June 2015 was the first International Day of Yoga.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The first Khelo India School Games were held in 2018 at
The first edition was held in New Delhi from 31 January 2018. Later editions, renamed Khelo India Youth Games, were held at Pune (2019), Guwahati (2020) and Panchkula (2021 edition held in 2022).
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Which of the following is NOT one of the four objectives of physical education given by Charles Bucher?
Bucher listed physical (organic), motor and movement, mental (cognitive) and social development. Economic development is not among them.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Franz Nachtegall is regarded as the father of physical education in

Nachtegall opened a private gymnasium in Copenhagen in 1799 and made Denmark the first European country to require physical education in schools. Sweden is linked with Ling, Germany with Jahn and England with games and sports.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Who is called the grandfather of gymnastics?
Guts Muths taught at Schnepfenthal for about fifty years and wrote Gymnastics for the Young (1793). Jahn, who built on his work, is the father of gymnastics.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
In Kretschmer's classification, a short, round and stout person is called
Kretschmer described pyknic (stout), athletic (muscular) and asthenic or leptosomatic (thin) types. Mesomorph belongs to Sheldon's classification.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
Hanuman Vyayam Prasarak Mandal, a pioneer institution of Indian physical culture, is located at
HVPM was founded at Amravati, Maharashtra in 1914 by the Vaidya brothers and promoted indigenous exercises. Gwalior houses LNIPE.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The first National Sports Policy of India was announced in
The National Sports Policy was first framed in 1984 and revised in 2001. 1968 and 1986 (with the 1992 Programme of Action) are years of national education policies.
History, Principles and Foundation of Physical Education
The ultimate aim of physical education is
Physical education aims at the wholesome development of the individual: physical, mental, emotional and social. Medals, muscles and military fitness are narrow outcomes, not the aim.
The number of bones in the adult human body is
An adult has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300, many of which fuse during growth.
How many bones form the axial skeleton?
The axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum and hyoid) has 80 bones. The appendicular skeleton (limbs and girdles) has 126, giving 206 in all.
The number of cervical vertebrae in the human body is
There are 7 cervical, 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae, followed by 5 fused sacral and 4 fused coccygeal vertebrae.
The longest and strongest bone of the body is the
The femur or thigh bone is the longest. The tibia is the shin bone, the fibula lies beside it, and the humerus is the bone of the upper arm.
The smallest bone in the human body is the
The stapes (stirrup) of the middle ear is the smallest bone. Malleus and incus are the other two ear ossicles and are slightly larger. The patella is the knee cap.
How many pairs of ribs are called floating ribs?

Of the 12 pairs, the first 7 are true ribs attached directly to the sternum, the next 3 are false ribs attached through cartilage, and the last 2 (11th and 12th) are floating ribs with free front ends.
The shoulder and hip are examples of which type of joint?

In a ball and socket joint the rounded head of one bone fits into a cup of another, allowing movement in all planes. The elbow and knee are hinge joints, and the joint between atlas and axis is a pivot joint.
A hinge joint allows movement in one plane only, flexion and extension, like a door hinge. The saddle joint is found at the base of the thumb.
The joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae, which lets the head turn, is a
A pivot joint permits rotation around one axis. The same type is found between the radius and ulna. Fibrous joints such as skull sutures are immovable.
The largest muscle of the human body is the
The gluteus maximus of the buttock is the largest single muscle by mass. The sartorius is the longest muscle, and the quadriceps is a group of four muscles.
Heart muscle has stripes like skeletal muscle but works without conscious control. Skeletal muscle is voluntary and striated; smooth muscle is involuntary and non-striated.
Tendons are tough cords that attach muscles to bones. Ligaments connect bone to bone at joints.
The sliding filament theory of muscle contraction was proposed by

H.E. Huxley and A.F. Huxley (working separately, 1954) explained that actin filaments slide over myosin filaments. A.V. Hill studied muscle heat and oxygen debt, William Harvey discovered blood circulation, and Sherrington studied reflexes.
Cardiac output is the product of
Cardiac output is the blood pumped by a ventricle in one minute: about 70 ml x 72 beats, roughly 5 litres at rest. Tidal volume x breathing rate gives minute ventilation, not cardiac output.
Normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is about
120 is the systolic and 80 the diastolic pressure. 140/90 and above indicates hypertension, and readings around 90/60 or lower indicate low blood pressure.
The volume of air breathed in or out in one normal breath is called
Tidal volume is about 500 ml. Vital capacity is the maximum air exhaled after a maximum inhalation, and residual volume is the air left in the lungs after a forced exhalation.
The average life span of a red blood cell is about
Red cells live about 120 days and are then destroyed in the spleen and liver. Platelets survive for roughly a week to ten days.
Which blood group is called the universal donor?
Group O (strictly O negative) red cells carry no A or B antigens and can be given to all groups. AB is the universal recipient.
Which gland is called the master gland of the body?
The pituitary, at the base of the brain, controls other endocrine glands. The thyroid regulates metabolism, the adrenals release adrenaline, and the pancreas secretes insulin.
Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas release insulin, which lowers blood sugar. Lack of it causes diabetes mellitus.
Which part of the brain controls balance and muscular coordination?

The cerebellum coordinates posture, balance and skilled movement. The cerebrum handles thinking and voluntary action, the medulla controls breathing and heartbeat, and the hypothalamus regulates temperature and hunger.
The main energy system used in a 100 m sprint is the

The phosphagen (ATP-PC) system supplies energy for all-out efforts up to about 10 seconds without oxygen or lactate. The lactic acid system dominates efforts up to about 2 minutes, and the aerobic system dominates long events.
Exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the
Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse. The trachea and bronchi are only air passages.
Which cell organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
Mitochondria produce ATP through aerobic respiration. The nucleus controls the cell, ribosomes make proteins and the Golgi body packages them.
Slow twitch (Type I) muscle fibres are best suited for

Slow twitch fibres are red, rich in mitochondria and myoglobin, and resist fatigue, so they suit distance running. Fast twitch (Type II) fibres produce quick, powerful contractions for sprints, lifts and jumps.
The natural pacemaker of the heart is the
The SA node in the right atrium starts each heartbeat. The impulse then passes to the AV node, bundle of His and Purkinje fibres, which conduct it through the ventricles.
The concept of oxygen debt was given by
A.V. Hill, a Nobel laureate, described the extra oxygen consumed after exercise to repay the deficit. Cooper is known for aerobics, Harvey for circulation and Selye for stress theory.
According to WHO, health is a state of complete
The 1948 WHO constitution defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. The other options cover only part of this.
World Health Day is observed on
7 April marks the founding of WHO in 1948. 5 June is World Environment Day, 1 December is World AIDS Day and 31 May is World No Tobacco Day.
Malaria is spread by the bite of the
The female Anopheles carries the Plasmodium parasite. Aedes spreads dengue and chikungunya, and Culex spreads filariasis.
Aedes aegypti, a day-biting mosquito that breeds in clean stagnant water, spreads the dengue virus. The sandfly spreads kala-azar and the tsetse fly spreads sleeping sickness.
TB is a bacterial disease that mainly affects the lungs and spreads through air. Salmonella typhi causes typhoid, Vibrio cholerae causes cholera and Plasmodium causes malaria.
The BCG vaccine is given to prevent
BCG stands for Bacillus Calmette-Guerin and is given at birth against tuberculosis. Polio is prevented by OPV or IPV, and tetanus by tetanus toxoid.
Which of the following is a water-borne disease?
Cholera spreads through water and food contaminated with Vibrio cholerae. Malaria is vector-borne, tuberculosis is air-borne and tetanus enters through wounds.
Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, which destroys T-helper cells. HPV causes cervical cancer, HBV causes hepatitis B and H1N1 causes swine flu.
An exaggerated backward curve of the upper (thoracic) spine producing a round back is called
Kyphosis is also called round back or hunch back. Lordosis is an increased forward curve of the lumbar spine, and scoliosis is a sideways curve.
An increased inward curve of the lumbar spine is known as
Lordosis, or hollow back, pushes the abdomen forward. Kyphosis affects the upper back and scoliosis bends the spine sideways into a C or S shape.
A sideways (lateral) curvature of the spine is called
Scoliosis may be C-shaped or S-shaped. Genu valgum is knock knees, a deformity of the legs, not the spine.
Genu valgum is the medical name for
In knock knees the knees touch while the ankles stay apart. Bow legs are called genu varum, and flat foot is pes planus.
Which of the following is a non-communicable disease?
Diabetes is a lifestyle or metabolic disorder and does not spread from person to person. The other three are infectious diseases.
World Environment Day is celebrated on
5 June has been observed since 1973 following the 1972 Stockholm Conference. 22 April is Earth Day and 16 September is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.
The intensity of sound is measured in
Decibel (dB) measures loudness. Hertz measures frequency, lux measures illumination and pascal measures pressure.
The gas mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect is
Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the major greenhouse gas, along with methane and nitrous oxide. Oxygen and nitrogen do not trap heat in the same way.
The first United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was held in 1972 at
The Stockholm Conference led to the creation of UNEP. Rio hosted the Earth Summit in 1992, the Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997 and the Paris Agreement in 2015.
The Environment (Protection) Act was passed in India in
The Act was passed in 1986 after the Bhopal gas tragedy. 1972 is the Wildlife Protection Act and 1981 is the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act.
The three main components of a school health programme are health services, healthful school living and
Health instruction (health education) gives knowledge and builds habits. Together with health services and a healthy environment it forms the school health programme.
The ozone layer protects the earth from
Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs most harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) deplete it.
The first aim of first aid is to
First aid aims to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening and promote recovery until medical help arrives. Diagnosis and prescription are a doctor's job.
The 3 Rs of waste management stand for
Reducing waste, reusing articles and recycling materials conserve resources and cut pollution.
World AIDS Day is observed on
1 December has been World AIDS Day since 1988. 14 November is World Diabetes Day and 31 May is World No Tobacco Day.
Typhoid is a bacterial infection of the intestine spread by contaminated food and water. Clostridium tetani causes tetanus and Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery.
The Paris Agreement of 2015 deals with
The Paris Agreement commits countries to hold global warming well below 2 degrees C above pre-industrial levels. It followed the Kyoto Protocol of 1997.
Flat foot is a deformity in which
The arch of the foot is lost
The ankle is twisted outward permanently
In flat foot (pes planus) the medial longitudinal arch collapses and the whole sole touches the ground. Walking on toes, picking marbles with toes and skipping help to correct it.
The word "yoga" is derived from the Sanskrit root "yuj", which means
Yuj means to yoke or join, signifying the union of the individual self with the universal self, or of body and mind.
The Yoga Sutras were compiled by
Patanjali systematised yoga in 195 or 196 sutras. Swatmarama wrote the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, Gheranda the Gheranda Samhita, and Vivekananda popularised Raja Yoga in the modern era.
How many limbs are there in Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga?
Ashta means eight: yama, niyama, asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana and samadhi.
The first limb of Ashtanga Yoga is
Yama (social restraints) comes first, followed by niyama (personal observances), asana and pranayama.
Which of the following is NOT a yama?
The five yamas are ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya and aparigraha. Santosha (contentment) is a niyama.
Aparigraha is not hoarding more than one needs. Ahimsa is non-violence, satya is truthfulness and asteya is non-stealing.
In pranayama, the stage of inhalation is called
Puraka is breathing in, kumbhaka is holding the breath and rechaka is breathing out. A bandha is a muscular lock.
Retention of breath in pranayama is known as
Kumbhaka may be internal (after inhaling) or external (after exhaling). Puraka and rechaka are inhalation and exhalation.
How many shatkarmas (cleansing processes) are described in Hatha Yoga?
Shat means six: neti, dhauti, basti, nauli, trataka and kapalbhati.
Steady gazing at a point or flame
Trataka cleanses the eyes and improves concentration. Neti cleans the nose, nauli churns the abdomen and dhauti cleans the stomach.
Jala neti is used to clean the
In jala neti, lukewarm saline water is passed through one nostril and out of the other. Dhauti is for the stomach and basti for the colon.
In Jalandhara bandha the chin is pressed against the chest. Uddiyana is the abdominal lock and Mula bandha is the root or anal lock.
Surya Namaskar consists of how many postures?
One round has twelve positions performed in sequence, each traditionally linked with a mantra of the sun.
The International Day of Yoga is observed on
21 June, the summer solstice, was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in December 2014 on India's proposal.
The first International Day of Yoga was celebrated in
The UN resolution was passed on 11 December 2014 and the first celebration took place on 21 June 2015, with the main event at Rajpath, New Delhi.
Which asana can be practised immediately after taking meals?
Vajrasana (thunderbolt pose) aids digestion and is the only asana recommended just after food. Inverted and abdominal-pressure poses must be done on an empty stomach.
Shavasana (corpse pose) and Makarasana relax the body and mind. Meditative asanas are sitting poses such as Padmasana, and cultural asanas develop the body.
Which of the following is a meditative asana?
Padmasana, Sukhasana, Siddhasana and Vajrasana give a stable seat for meditation. The other three are cultural (corrective) asanas for the spine.
The Hatha Yoga Pradipika was written by
Swatmarama composed this classic text on asana, pranayama, mudra and samadhi in about the 15th century. Vyasa wrote a commentary on the Yoga Sutras.
Cooper, a US Air Force physician, published the book Aerobics in 1968. Jane Fonda later popularised workout videos, and Pilates created a different exercise system.
The commonly used formula for estimating maximum heart rate is
A 20-year-old thus has an estimated maximum of 200 beats per minute. Training zones are set as a percentage of this figure.
"Yogah karmasu kaushalam" (yoga is skill in action) is a statement from the
The line occurs in chapter 2 of the Gita. Patanjali's definition in the Yoga Sutras is "Yogas chitta vritti nirodhah".
Dhyana, the seventh limb of Ashtanga Yoga, means
Dhyana is an unbroken flow of attention. Dharana is concentration, pratyahara is sense withdrawal and asana is posture.
The final stage of Ashtanga Yoga is
Samadhi is complete absorption, the eighth limb. Pratyahara, dharana and dhyana are the fifth, sixth and seventh limbs.
In which pranayama is a humming sound like a bee produced during exhalation?
Bhramari comes from bhramar, the black bee. Sheetali cools the body by inhaling through a rolled tongue, bhastrika is bellows breathing, and ujjayi produces a soft sound in the throat.
Which pranayama is known for its cooling effect on the body?
In Sheetali air is drawn in through the rolled tongue, cooling the body. Bhastrika and Suryabhedana generate heat, and Kapalbhati is a cleansing kriya.
The Karvonen formula for target heart rate uses the
Karvonen's method takes maximum heart rate minus resting heart rate (the reserve), multiplies it by the chosen intensity and adds the resting rate back.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
Microteaching was first developed at Stanford University in 1963 by

Dwight Allen and his colleagues designed microteaching to train teachers in one skill at a time. Skinner is known for programmed instruction, Dale for the Cone of Experience and Bloom for the taxonomy of objectives.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The Cone of Experience was given by
Edgar Dale presented the cone in 1946 to rank learning experiences from concrete to abstract. Gagne gave the conditions of learning and Bruner the discovery approach.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
At the base of Dale's Cone of Experience is
The base holds the most concrete learning, doing the real thing. The cone narrows upward to the most abstract level.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
At the top (apex) of Dale's Cone of Experience are
Verbal symbols, spoken or written words, are the most abstract experience. Field trips and demonstrations lie in the lower, more concrete bands.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The correct order of the microteaching cycle is
Feedback, plan, teach, re-feedback, re-plan, re-teach
Teach, plan, feedback, re-teach, re-plan, re-feedback
Plan, feedback, teach, re-plan, re-feedback, re-teach
Plan, teach, feedback, re-plan, re-teach, re-feedback
The trainee plans a short lesson, teaches it, receives feedback, then revises and repeats. The Indian model allots about 36 minutes to one cycle.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
In microteaching, the class usually consists of
Microteaching is scaled down in class size (5 to 10), time (5 to 10 minutes) and content (one skill).
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The hardware approach to educational technology refers to the use of
The hardware approach applies engineering products such as projectors, computers and television. The software approach applies learning principles, and the systems approach applies management ideas.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The software approach in educational technology is based on
Behavioural sciences and the psychology of learning
It concerns instructional design, programmed learning, task analysis and reinforcement, drawn mainly from the work of Skinner and others.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
Programmed instruction (linear type) is associated with
Skinner's linear programme presents small frames with immediate reinforcement. Crowder developed branching programmes, Gilbert mathetics, and Pressey the first teaching machine.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The spectrum of teaching styles in physical education was proposed by
Mosston's spectrum runs from the command style, where the teacher makes all decisions, to learner-initiated styles.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
In Mosston's reciprocal style of teaching
Learners work in pairs and one gives feedback to the other
Learners discover the answer through questions
Each learner checks his own work
One partner performs while the other observes with a criteria sheet. The teacher-decides option is the command style, self-checking is the self-check style and questioning is guided discovery.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The command method of teaching is
In the command method the teacher gives orders and the class responds together. It suits drill, marching and large classes but gives little room for individual thinking.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The whole method of teaching is most suitable for
Simple skills that cannot be divided
Simple, continuous skills such as running or a forward roll are best taught whole. Complex skills with separable parts are taught by the part or whole-part-whole method.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The parts of a command in the correct order are
The explanatory part tells what is to be done, the pause allows preparation, and the executive word signals the moment of action.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
In the command "Class, right turn", the word "turn" is the
"Class, right" explains what is to be done and "turn" is the sharp executive word on which the movement is performed.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
For exercises performed continuously to counts
Rhythmic commands such as "one-two-three-four" keep the class exercising in unison. Response commands are for single actions like "attention".
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
Which of the following is an audio-visual aid?
Television appeals to both ear and eye. A chart and a model are visual aids, and radio is an audio aid.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
A chart showing the measurements of a volleyball court is a
Charts, diagrams, models and blackboards are seen, not heard, so they are visual aids.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The first part of a physical education lesson is the
The lesson opens with assembly and warm-up, moves to the formal or skill part, then a recreative game, and ends with the concluding part.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The main purpose of a lead-up game is to
Practise a skill in a simplified game situation
Lead-up games use modified rules so that learners apply the new skill and move toward the full game.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The best class formation for giving a demonstration is usually a
Closed circle with the teacher outside
In a semicircle every pupil can see and hear the teacher. In a single file those at the back cannot see.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The formal steps of teaching (Herbartian steps) begin with
Herbart's followers listed preparation, presentation, association (comparison), generalisation and application.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The imitation method of teaching is most suitable for
Small children learn by copying, as in mimetic exercises (hop like a frog, fly like a bird).
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The teacher's personal preparation for a lesson includes
Proper dress, voice and knowledge of the subject
Personal preparation concerns the teacher. Marking and equipment are technical preparation.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
The first teaching machine was devised by
Pressey built a testing and teaching machine in the 1920s. Skinner later developed teaching machines based on operant conditioning.
Educational Technology and Methods of Teaching in Physical Education
In CAI the computer presents material, asks questions and gives immediate feedback.
POSDCORB, a statement of the functions of administration, was coined by
Gulick listed planning, organising, staffing, directing, coordinating, reporting and budgeting. Fayol gave 14 principles, Taylor scientific management and Drucker management by objectives.
In POSDCORB, the letter "B" stands for
Budgeting covers fiscal planning, accounting and control.
In a knock-out tournament of 16 teams, the total number of matches will be
Matches in a knock-out equal N minus 1, since every match eliminates one team and one champion remains.
How many byes are given in a knock-out fixture of 11 teams?
Byes equal the next higher power of two minus the number of teams: 16 minus 11 is 5.
In a knock-out tournament of 19 teams, the number of byes is
The next power of two above 19 is 32, and 32 minus 19 is 13.
The number of matches in a single league tournament of 6 teams is
Single league matches are N(N minus 1)/2, which is 6 x 5 / 2 = 15. A double league would have 30.
How many matches are played in a double league tournament of 5 teams?
A double league has N(N minus 1) matches: 5 x 4 = 20. A single league of 5 teams has 10.
How many rounds are there in a knock-out tournament of 16 teams?
16 is 2 to the power 4, so there are four rounds: round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals and final.
How many rounds will be played in a knock-out tournament of 20 teams?
Rounds equal the power of two that just covers the entries: 32 is 2 to the power 5.
In a knock-out fixture of 13 teams, how many teams are placed in the upper half?
With an odd number, the upper half gets (N+1)/2 = 7 and the lower half (N minus 1)/2 = 6.
In a knock-out fixture of 11 teams with 5 byes, how many byes go to the lower half?
When the number of byes is odd, the lower half gets (byes + 1)/2 = 3 and the upper half gets 2.
The purpose of seeding in a tournament is to
Keep strong teams apart in the early rounds
Seeded teams are placed in different halves or quarters so that they do not meet before the later rounds.
A bye in a tournament is given in the
A bye lets a team move to the second round without playing in the first, so that the numbers work out to a power of two.
Intra means within and muralis means wall. Intramural competitions take place among students of the same institution.
Competitions between two or more institutions are called
Extramural means outside the walls. They give selected players higher competition.
Which of the following is NOT a method of drawing a league fixture?
Cyclic, staircase and tabular are methods of the round-robin tournament. The ladder is a type of challenge tournament.
Ladder and pyramid are types of
In a challenge tournament a player may challenge someone placed above and change places on winning.
The 14 principles of management were given by
Fayol's principles include division of work, unity of command and scalar chain. Mayo led the Hawthorne studies and Weber described bureaucracy.
Who is called the father of scientific management?
Frederick Winslow Taylor introduced time and motion study. Fayol is called the father of modern (administrative) management.
A budget is a statement of
Estimated income and expenditure for a fixed period
A budget is a financial plan, normally for one year, that estimates receipts and planned spending.
The register in which all non-consumable equipment purchased is recorded is the
The stock register records each article with date, quantity and cost. The issue register records what is given out for daily use.
The chief purpose of supervision in physical education is
Improvement of teaching and the programme
Modern supervision is democratic and guiding. Fault-finding inspection is the outdated view.
"Unity of command" means that an employee should receive orders from
This Fayol principle prevents confusion and conflicting instructions.
An outdoor playfield should ideally be laid out in which direction?
A north-south orientation keeps the rising and setting sun out of the players' eyes.
A consolation tournament is organised to
Give defeated teams another chance to play
In a consolation tournament teams beaten in the first round (or first match) continue in a second bracket.
The number of rounds in a single league tournament of 8 teams is
For an even number of teams the rounds are N minus 1. For an odd number they equal N.
The Dronacharya Award is given to
Instituted in 1985, it honours coaches who have produced medal winners. The Arjuna Award is for players.
The Arjuna Award was instituted in
The Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports began in 1961. 1985 is the Dronacharya Award, 1991-92 the Khel Ratna and 2002 the Dhyan Chand Award.
The first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (1991-92) was
Chess grandmaster Viswanathan Anand received the first award. Geet Sethi received it the following year and Tendulkar in 1997-98.
In 2021 the Khel Ratna Award was renamed after
It is now the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, India's highest sporting honour.
The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy is awarded to the
Best state in the National Games
Started in 1956-57, it goes to the university with the best all-round performance in inter-university, national and international competitions.
The Dhyan Chand Award, instituted in 2002, is given for
It honours sportspersons for lifetime contribution, including after retirement. Adventure is recognised by the Tenzing Norgay Award and companies by the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar.
A coach who takes all decisions alone and expects obedience follows the
The autocratic or command style is coach-centred. The democratic style involves athletes in decisions, and laissez-faire leaves them largely to themselves.
A coach who involves players in decision making follows the
The democratic or cooperative style shares decisions while the coach still guides.
The plan made before the season
The correct way of performing a movement
The fitness level of a player
Technique is the efficient motor procedure for a sports task. A plan for the season is strategy.
Plans and actions used during a match to gain an advantage over the opponent are called
Tactics are applied in the competition situation. Strategy is the broader plan made beforehand.
The most essential quality of a good official is
An official must be fair to both sides, in addition to knowing the rules and being fit.
Which is a duty of an official before the start of a match?
Checking the playing area and equipment
Signing the score sheet as final
Pre-game duties include inspecting the field, equipment and players' kit and conducting the toss. Signing the score sheet and reports come after the game.
The "advantage" rule in games such as football and hockey means the referee
Lets play continue when stopping it would benefit the offending team
Gives extra time to the losing team
Awards a goal to the fouled team
Play is allowed to go on if the non-offending side would gain more from continuing.
Coaching differs from teaching mainly because coaching
Aims at high performance of selected players
Teaching gives basic skills to all; coaching refines skill and prepares selected performers for competition.
O.M. Nambiar was among the first recipients of the Dronacharya Award in 1985. Achrekar coached Sachin Tendulkar and Gopichand coached Saina Nehwal and P.V. Sindhu.
The Tenzing Norgay National Award is given for excellence in
It recognises achievement in adventure on land, water and in the air, and is treated as equivalent to the Arjuna Award.
The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar (2009) is awarded to
It recognises companies, sports control boards and NGOs for identifying talent, supporting sportspersons and sports development.
The first woman to receive the Khel Ratna Award was
Weightlifter Karnam Malleswari received it for 1994-95. Anju Bobby George and Mary Kom received it later.
The coaching philosophy "Athletes first, winning second" is associated with
Rainer Martens, author of Successful Coaching, promoted this athlete-centred philosophy.
Information given to a performer about the quality of the movement itself is called
Knowledge of performance concerns how the movement was done. Knowledge of results concerns the outcome, such as distance or score.
In most games, protests against decisions are finally decided by the
A jury of appeal or technical committee is appointed for each competition to settle protests under the rules.
A good official's decisions should be
Quick, confident and uniform decisions earn the respect of players and keep control of the game.
The first step in a long-term coaching programme is
Coaching begins by spotting children with potential, followed by basic, build-up and high-performance training.
The Dronacharya Award was instituted in
It was first given in 1985. The first recipients included O.M. Nambiar (athletics), Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat (wrestling) and Om Prakash Bhardwaj (boxing).
The study of signals, positioning and teamwork among officials is known as
Mechanics covers where officials stand and move, how they signal and how they share duties.
A half-time talk by the coach should mainly
Give a few clear corrections and encouragement
Explain the history of the game
Players can absorb only a few points in a short interval, so the coach concentrates on key adjustments.
The ancient Olympic Games are traditionally said to have begun in
The first recorded Games were held at Olympia in 776 BC. 490 BC is the Battle of Marathon and 1896 the first modern Games.
The ancient Olympic Games were held in honour of
Olympia was the sanctuary of Zeus. The Pythian Games honoured Apollo and the Isthmian Games honoured Poseidon.
The ancient Olympic Games were abolished by the Roman Emperor
Theodosius I banned pagan festivals in about 393-394 AD, ending the Games.
The father of the modern Olympic Games is
The French educationist Baron de Coubertin revived the Games. Vikelas was the first IOC President and Guttmann founded the Paralympic movement.
The International Olympic Committee was founded on
The IOC was created at the Sorbonne congress in Paris. 23 June is celebrated as Olympic Day. 6 April 1896 was the opening of the Athens Games.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 at
Athens hosted in 1896, followed by Paris (1900), St Louis (1904) and London (1908).
The headquarters of the IOC is at
The IOC moved to Lausanne in 1915. It was founded in Paris.
The first President of the IOC was
Vikelas of Greece served from 1894 to 1896. Coubertin succeeded him and served until 1925.
The word added to the Olympic motto in 2021 is
The motto became Citius, Altius, Fortius, Communiter, meaning Faster, Higher, Stronger, Together.
The original Olympic motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius" was coined by
Didon, a Dominican priest and friend of Coubertin, used it for a school sports event. Bishop Talbot inspired the creed about taking part.
Which of these colours is NOT found in the Olympic rings?
The five rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background.
The Olympic flag was first hoisted at the Games of
The flag was designed by Coubertin in 1913 and first flown at Antwerp in 1920, where the Olympic oath was also first taken.
The Olympic torch relay was introduced at the Games of
The flame was first lit in the stadium at Amsterdam 1928, but the relay from Olympia started in 1936.
The first official Olympic mascot, Waldi the dachshund, appeared at
Waldi was the first official mascot of the Summer Games. Misha the bear was the mascot at Moscow 1980.
The first Winter Olympic Games were held in 1924 at
Chamonix, France hosted the first Winter Games. St Moritz hosted in 1928 and Lake Placid in 1932.
The first Paralympic Games were held in
Rome 1960 is recognised as the first Paralympics. In 1948 Sir Ludwig Guttmann organised the Stoke Mandeville Games, the forerunner.
The first Summer Youth Olympic Games were held in 2010 at
Singapore hosted in 2010, Nanjing in 2014 and Buenos Aires in 2018. Innsbruck hosted the first Winter Youth Olympics in 2012.
Women first took part in the modern Olympic Games at
Women competed in tennis and golf at Paris 1900. Women's athletics entered in 1928.
The Indian Olympic Association was formed in
The IOA was founded in 1927 with Sir Dorabji Tata as President and Dr A.G. Noehren as Secretary.
The first President of the Indian Olympic Association was
Sir Dorabji Tata financed India's early Olympic participation. Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala succeeded him.
Norman Pritchard won two silver medals for India at the Paris Olympics of
Pritchard won silver in the 200 m and 200 m hurdles in 1900, India's first Olympic medals.
India won its first Olympic hockey gold medal at
India won gold at six successive Games from 1928 to 1956 and has eight hockey golds in all.
The first individual Olympic medal for independent India was won by
Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav won bronze in wrestling at Helsinki 1952.
The first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal was
Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting (69 kg) at Sydney 2000. Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom won bronze medals in 2012.
India's first individual Olympic gold medal was won by Abhinav Bindra in
Bindra won the men's 10 m air rifle at Beijing. Neeraj Chopra won India's second individual gold in javelin at Tokyo 2020.
The first Asian Games were held in 1951 at
New Delhi hosted the first Asian Games; their motto is "Ever Onward". Manila hosted the second Games in 1954.
The first Commonwealth Games (then called British Empire Games) were held in 1930 at
Hamilton hosted the first edition. India hosted the Commonwealth Games at Delhi in 2010.
One gram of fat provides about
Fat is the most concentrated energy source at 9 kcal per gram. Carbohydrate and protein give 4 kcal per gram and alcohol about 7.
One gram of carbohydrate provides about
Carbohydrate, the body's main and quickest fuel, gives 4 kcal per gram, the same as protein.
The nutrient mainly responsible for growth and repair of tissues is
Proteins are body-building foods made of amino acids. Carbohydrates and fats are mainly energy-giving foods.
Scurvy is caused by deficiency of
Lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes bleeding gums and slow wound healing. Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.
Rickets in children is caused by deficiency of
Vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium; its lack produces soft, bent bones. In adults the same deficiency causes osteomalacia.
Night blindness results from deficiency of
Vitamin A (retinol) is needed for the visual pigment of the retina. Sources include carrots, green leafy vegetables and fish liver oil.
Beriberi is caused by lack of
Thiamine deficiency affects nerves and the heart. Niacin deficiency causes pellagra and B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.
Pellagra is caused by deficiency of
Pellagra shows the three Ds: dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia. Riboflavin deficiency causes cracks at the corners of the mouth.
Which vitamin helps in the clotting of blood?
Vitamin K is needed to make prothrombin. Its deficiency leads to prolonged bleeding.
Which of the following is a water-soluble vitamin?
Vitamins B complex and C dissolve in water and are not stored in large amounts. A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.
Deficiency of iron in the diet causes
Iron is part of haemoglobin; its lack reduces oxygen-carrying capacity and causes tiredness. Goitre is due to iodine deficiency.
Goitre is caused by deficiency of
Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine. Iodised salt prevents goitre.
Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated as
Weight in kg multiplied by height in metres
Height in metres divided by weight in kg
Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared
BMI = kg/m2. Waist divided by hip gives the waist-hip ratio, a different index.
According to WHO, a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 is classified as
Below 18.5 is underweight, 25 to 29.9 is overweight and 30 or above is obese.
A person is classified as obese when the BMI is
WHO defines obesity as a BMI of 30 or more, with classes I, II and III at 30, 35 and 40.
Carbohydrate loading is used mainly by athletes in
Endurance events such as the marathon
Raising muscle glycogen stores in the days before competition delays fatigue in events lasting more than about 90 minutes.
Carbohydrate is stored in the body in the liver and muscles as
Glycogen is the animal storage form. Starch and cellulose are plant carbohydrates.
The energy required by the body at complete rest to maintain vital functions is called
BMR accounts for the largest share of daily energy use. Specific dynamic action is the energy cost of digesting food.
The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) was established in
WADA was set up on 10 November 1999 at Lausanne after the 1998 Tour de France scandal. Its code came into force in 2004.
The headquarters of WADA is at
WADA moved from Lausanne to Montreal in 2002. Lausanne is the home of the IOC.
Erythropoietin (EPO) is misused by endurance athletes because it
EPO is a peptide hormone that raises the red cell count and thus oxygen transport. Diuretics reduce weight, beta-blockers calm tremor and anabolic steroids build muscle.
Diuretics are banned in sport because they
Cause rapid weight loss and mask other drugs
Diuretics increase urine output, helping athletes make weight and diluting traces of other banned substances.
About 20 amino acids form body proteins, of which 9 are essential and must come from food. Fats are made of fatty acids and glycerol.
Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by deficiency of
Kwashiorkor shows swelling (oedema), a pot belly and skin and hair changes in young children. Marasmus is due to overall deficiency of energy and protein.
Which vitamin is produced in the skin in the presence of sunlight?
Ultraviolet rays convert a cholesterol compound in the skin into vitamin D, hence the name sunshine vitamin.
The pre-competition meal should be taken about
A light, carbohydrate-rich, low-fat meal 3 to 4 hours before allows digestion and tops up energy stores.
The mineral most important for strong bones and teeth is
About 99 percent of body calcium is in bones and teeth. Milk and milk products are the best sources.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The width of each lane on a standard athletics track is
Each lane is 1.22 m wide, including the 5 cm line on its right.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The length of a standard running track measured in lane 1 is
The standard outdoor track is 400 m. Indoor tracks are 200 m.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
On a standard 400 m track, the length of each straight is
The standard track has two straights of 84.39 m and two semicircular bends of radius 36.50 m.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The radius of the bends of a standard 400 m track is
With a 36.50 m radius and the measuring line 30 cm out, each bend is 115.61 m long.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The marathon is run over a distance of
The distance of 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards) was fixed after the 1908 London Olympics.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The height of the hurdles in the men's 110 m hurdles is
Men's 110 m hurdles are 1.067 m (3 ft 6 in). 0.914 m is used in the men's 400 m hurdles, 0.838 m in the women's 100 m hurdles and 0.762 m in the women's 400 m hurdles.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The height of the hurdles in the women's 100 m hurdles is
Women's sprint hurdles are 0.838 m (2 ft 9 in) high.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
How many hurdles does an athlete clear in a 400 m hurdles race?
All standard hurdle races (100 m, 110 m and 400 m) have 10 flights.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
In the 3000 m steeplechase, the number of water jumps is
There are 7 water jumps and 28 hurdle jumps, 35 clearances in all.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
In the men's 110 m hurdles, the distance from the start line to the first hurdle is
The run to the first hurdle is 13.72 m, the spacing between hurdles is 9.14 m and the run-in is 14.02 m. In the women's 100 m hurdles the first hurdle is at 13 m.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The length of a relay baton is
The baton is a smooth hollow tube 28 to 30 cm long weighing at least 50 g.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The length of the take-over zone in the 4 x 100 m relay is
Since 2018 the old 10 m acceleration zone has been merged into a single 30 m take-over zone for the 4 x 100 m. The 4 x 400 m zone is 20 m.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
For races of 800 m and longer, the starter's commands are
"On your marks", "Set" and then the gun
"On your marks" and then the gun
There is no "Set" command in races longer than 400 m because a standing start is used.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
A reaction time faster than how many seconds is treated as a false start?
Starting blocks linked to the start information system record reaction time; under 0.100 s is judged to be anticipation.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The finish of a race is decided when which part of the body reaches the finish line?
The torso (trunk) counts, not the head, neck, arms, legs, hands or feet.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
A record in the 100 m is not accepted if the following wind exceeds
The 2.0 m/s limit applies to the 100 m, 200 m, sprint hurdles, long jump and triple jump.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The Fosbury flop technique of high jump was introduced by Dick Fosbury at the Olympics of
Fosbury won gold in 1968 going over the bar backwards. Earlier styles were the scissors, western roll and straddle.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The correct sequence of phases in the triple jump is
The athlete takes off and lands on the same foot (hop), then lands on the other foot (step), and finally jumps into the pit.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The width of the take-off board in the long jump is
The board is 1.22 m long, 20 cm wide and up to 10 cm deep, painted white.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The length of the crossbar in the high jump is
The high jump bar is 4.00 m long. The pole vault bar is 4.50 m.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
A high jumper is eliminated after
Three failures in total at any heights
Three failures in a row, regardless of the heights at which they occur, end the competition for that athlete.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The men's 100 m world record of 9.58 s was set in 2009 by
Bolt of Jamaica ran 9.58 at the Berlin World Championships, where he also set the 200 m record of 19.19 s.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The men's long jump world record of 8.95 m (1991) is held by
Powell broke Bob Beamon's 8.90 m (1968) at the Tokyo World Championships.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
The IAAF changed its name to World Athletics in
The body was founded in 1912 as the International Amateur Athletic Federation and has been called World Athletics since 2019.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
Who is known as the "Flying Sikh"?
Milkha Singh finished fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics and won Commonwealth and Asian Games gold medals.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
On a track, races are run in which direction?
Runners keep the inside of the track on their left, running anticlockwise.
Track and Field (Running and Jumping Events)
In long jump with more than eight competitors, each athlete first gets
All get three trials and the best eight get three more. With eight or fewer competitors each gets six.
The length of an Olympic-size swimming pool is
Long-course pools are 50 m long and 25 m wide. Short-course pools are 25 m long.
The width of each lane in an Olympic swimming pool is
Each lane is 2.5 m wide. 1.22 m is the lane width of an athletics track.
The correct order of strokes in the individual medley is
The individual medley begins with butterfly. The medley relay has a different order starting with backstroke.
In a medley relay, the first swimmer swims
The relay order is backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle, because the backstroke start is taken from the water.
In which stroke do swimmers start from inside the water?
Backstrokers hold the starting grips with their feet on the wall. All other strokes use a dive from the block.
The fastest swimming stroke is the
The front crawl is the fastest and breaststroke the slowest of the four competitive strokes.
The international federation for swimming, earlier known as FINA, is now called
FINA, founded in 1908, adopted the name World Aquatics from 2023.
How many apparatus are there in men's artistic gymnastics?
Men compete on floor, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar. Women have 4 apparatus.
How many apparatus are there in women's artistic gymnastics?
Women compete on vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor.
Which of the following is NOT a men's gymnastics apparatus?
The balance beam is for women only. Pommel horse, rings and parallel bars are men's apparatus.
The width of the balance beam is
The beam is 5 m long, 10 cm wide and 125 cm above the floor.
The floor exercise area in gymnastics measures
The sprung floor performance area is 12 m square.
The Federation Internationale de Gymnastique (FIG), the oldest international sports federation, was founded in
FIG was founded in 1881 at Liege, Belgium. Its headquarters is now in Lausanne.
The first gymnast to score a perfect 10 at the Olympics was
Nadia Comaneci of Romania scored 10 on the uneven bars at Montreal 1976, aged 14.
Dipa Karmakar finished fourth at the Rio 2016 Olympics in
She became the first Indian woman gymnast at the Olympics and performed the difficult Produnova vault.
Which of these is NOT an apparatus of rhythmic gymnastics?
Rhythmic gymnastics uses rope, hoop, ball, clubs and ribbon. The pommel horse belongs to men's artistic gymnastics.
The International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) was founded in
The ISSF was founded in 1907 and has its headquarters at Munich. 1951 is the year of the National Rifle Association of India.
The calibre of air rifles and air pistols used in 10 m events is
Air weapons fire 4.5 mm (.177) pellets. 5.6 mm (.22) is used in 25 m and 50 m small-bore events.
Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won a silver medal at Athens 2004 in
Rathore's silver in men's double trap was India's first individual Olympic silver. Vijay Kumar won silver in 25 m rapid fire pistol in 2012.
Who became the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympic Games after independence, at Paris 2024?
Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10 m air pistol and in the 10 m air pistol mixed team with Sarabjot Singh.
Swapnil Kusale won a bronze medal at Paris 2024 in
Kusale became the first Indian to win an Olympic medal in the 50 m rifle 3 positions event.
Trap and skeet are events of
In trap and skeet, shooters fire shotguns at flying clay targets.
The kick used in the butterfly stroke is the
Both legs move together up and down in a dolphin kick. The flutter kick is used in freestyle and backstroke, and the whip (frog) kick in breaststroke.
In breaststroke and butterfly, the swimmer must touch the wall at turns and at the finish with
A one-hand touch in these strokes leads to disqualification. Freestyle and backstroke allow a touch with any part of the body or one hand.
The most decorated Olympian of all time, with 28 medals, is the swimmer
Phelps of the USA won 23 gold medals, including 8 at Beijing 2008. Mark Spitz won 7 golds at Munich 1972.
The National Rifle Association of India was founded in
NRAI was formed in 1951 to promote shooting sport in India. 1907 is the ISSF and 1927 the Indian Olympic Association.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The dimensions of a kabaddi court for men are
The men's court is 13 m by 10 m. The women's and junior court is 12 m by 8 m.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
How many players of a kabaddi team are on the court at a time?
Seven players play and five are substitutes, making a team of twelve.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The duration of a men's kabaddi match is
Men play 20 minutes each way with a 5 minute interval. Women and juniors play two halves of 15 minutes.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The maximum time allowed for a raid in kabaddi is
A raider must return to his own half within 30 seconds while keeping up the cant.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
A "lona" in kabaddi earns the scoring side
When all the opposing players are put out, the side scores two additional points and the opponents are revived.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
A bonus point in kabaddi can be attempted only when the defending side has at least
The bonus line is active when six or seven defenders are present. The raider must cross it with one foot while the other is in the air.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
A "super tackle" in kabaddi takes place when a raider is caught by a defence of
A successful tackle with three or fewer defenders on court earns one extra point, two in all.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
In men's kabaddi the baulk line is at what distance from the mid line?
The baulk line is 3.75 m from the mid line for men and 3 m for women. A raider must cross it for the raid to be valid, unless a touch is made.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Kabaddi was included as a medal sport in the Asian Games for the first time at
Kabaddi was a demonstration sport at New Delhi 1982 and a medal event from Beijing 1990.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The Pro Kabaddi League was started in
The franchise league began in 2014 and greatly increased the popularity of the game. 2008 is the first season of the Indian Premier League in cricket.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The word repeated continuously by a raider in kabaddi is called the
The cant is the clear, continuous chant of "kabaddi" in one breath. Kho is the word used in kho-kho.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Kabaddi is the national game of
Kabaddi (Ha-du-du) is Bangladesh's national game. Bhutan's national sport is archery and Sri Lanka's is volleyball.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The dimensions of a kho-kho field are
Under current Kho Kho Federation of India rules the field is 27 m by 16 m with two poles and eight cross lanes.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
How many players of a kho-kho team take the field?
Nine players play out of a team of twelve.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
At the start of a turn in kho-kho, how many chasers sit in the squares?
Eight chasers sit in the squares facing alternate directions and the ninth is the active chaser.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The duration of each turn in a kho-kho match is
A match has two innings; each innings has a chasing turn and a running turn of 9 minutes each.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
In kho-kho, defenders (runners) enter the field in batches of
The nine runners enter in three batches of three.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The Kho Kho Federation of India was founded in
KKFI was established in 1955 and the first national championship was held in 1959-60 at Vijayawada.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The first Kho Kho World Cup was held in January 2025 at
It was held at the Indira Gandhi Arena, New Delhi, and India won both the men's and women's titles.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Malla means wrestler and khamb means pole; the pole was originally a training aid for wrestlers.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Which of the following is NOT a type of mallakhamb?
The three competitive forms are fixed pole, hanging pole and rope mallakhamb.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Mallakhamb was declared the state sport of
Madhya Pradesh declared it the state sport in 2013, although the sport was revived in Maharashtra by Balambhatta Dada Deodhar.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Lezim is a traditional folk drill of
Lezim is performed in Maharashtra with a small wooden instrument fitted with jingling metal discs, to the beat of the dhol.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The pace of quick march in marching is about
Quick time is about 120 paces a minute. Slow march is about 60 to 70 and double march about 180.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
Savdhan is attention, vishram is stand at ease, tham is halt and visarjan is dismiss.
Indigenous Sports: Kabaddi / Mallakhamb / Kho-Kho, Lezim / March-past
The width of the lobby on each side of a kabaddi court is
The lobbies are 1 m strips on both sides which become part of the court only after a touch (struggle) begins.
Mass Demonstration Activities: Dumbbells, Tipri / Wands / Hoop / Umbrella
Tipri, used in mass demonstration, is
A pair of short wooden sticks
